acceptance.criterion_verbatim: A replayed (already-consumed) code shows an error and the user stays out -- not a spinner, not a silent retry.
acceptance.invocation: Run DISTINCTLY from DE2-2 rather than relabelled. The stub models CONSUMPTION: the first redemption of code 654321 marks the challenge consumed, and the SAME code thereafter finds nothing and returns 401 -- mirroring verifyAndConsumeChallenge(), which DELETES rather than flags. The same code was then submitted twice.
acceptance.output_evidence: The call log shows two verify requests with consumedAtCallTime false then TRUE, so the second genuinely hit a consumed challenge. On the replay: error shown ('Invalid or expired code'), still on /login, spinnerStuck FALSE, field cleared, localStorage.accessToken null throughout. Total verify requests 2 for 2 deliberate submits -- exactly one per submit, so there was NO silent retry.
acceptance.denominator: 2 submits, 2 verify requests. A silent retry would have produced 3 or more.
acceptance.status_reason: BOUNDED: the DELETION is a SERVER property, exercised by W1-5, not by me. What this run establishes is the CLIENT half -- a replay surfaces as an error, keeps the user out, leaves no spinner running, and triggers no automatic resubmit. The component guards the double-submit with an explicit early return on isSubmitting rather than relying on the disabled attribute alone, because against the real handler a second in-flight submit would burn a code that had just worked.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: Resend issues a new code and the previous one no longer works.
acceptance.invocation: All 16 routes of auth-handler/src/index.ts read; src/mfa.ts exports enumerated; call sites of issueChallenge traced.
acceptance.output_evidence: There is no resend endpoint and no standalone issuer. issueChallenge() has exactly ONE call site, inside login(). The only way to mint a new code today is to call /auth/login again -- which requires the PASSWORD again. A Resend built on that would have to retain the password in client state, which DE2-5 forbids, and would re-run the WS-1 login throttle counter keyed on the submitted email.
acceptance.denominator: 16 of 16 routes read; 2 of 2 mfa.ts exports enumerated; 1 of 1 issueChallenge call sites.
acceptance.status_reason: AMENDED 2026-09-01 ~03:2xZ. THE CONSTRUCTION BLOCKER IS RETIRED: W3 Act A landed (0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Z, e96de00837) and POST /auth/mfa/send is LIVE, confirmed by my own probe against the production host -- 200 {success:true}, the handler's body not the gateway's. So this row is no longer blocked BY CONSTRUCTION; the Resend control has a real endpoint and calls it. What remains is an instrument gap, hence the status change rather than a PASS. TWO THINGS ARE STILL MISSING AND BOTH ARE NAMED: (1) a test subject, so no real challenge has been re-issued; (2) A SCORING TRAP FOR WHOEVER VERIFIES THIS ROW LATER, and it is the important half -- /auth/mfa/send RETURNS 200 {success:true} FOR A challengeId THAT DOES NOT EXIST. I measured that with challengeId probe-nonexistent. It is DELIBERATE, not a defect: enumeration-safety, evidenced by 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Z's {event: mfa_resend_refused} log line, which is what proves the refusal path RAN rather than the route being an inert no-op (1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z 17719 s.2). CONSEQUENCE: SENT AND REFUSED ARE THE SAME HTTP RESPONSE. Anything scoring this route from HTTP alone is scoring a CONSTANT and would return PASS against a completely broken route. The log line is the ONLY plane on which the two differ, and it is not on my surface. NOT SCORED AS PASS. The 'Send a new code' control exists and is wired to requestMfaCode() -> POST /auth/mfa/send -- the same endpoint DE1-1 needs -- so the row passes with no further frontend change once issuance is split out of login(). The second half, 'the previous one no longer works', is a SERVER property that will follow from re-issuing the challenge; I have not exercised it and do not claim it. Proposed owner 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Z; routed to 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z as msg 17360.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: NEGATIVE: the code appears in no URL, no console log, no analytics payload and no persisted client state. Enumerate where you looked and carry a positive control proving the search would have found it.
acceptance.invocation: After submitting code 123456, every candidate carrier was read out of the live page and tested for the literal code, beside a planted positive control.
acceptance.output_evidence: ENUMERATED, all false: window.location.href (len 27); localStorage serialised whole (len 112 -- non-empty, so the search had real content to miss); sessionStorage (len 0); document.cookie (len 0); window.history.state (len 51); the DOM input value (cleared, len 0). Every browser console message was dumped -- 55 of 55, level info, all:true -- and none contains the code. POSITIVE CONTROL: the same matcher run against a planted string of the same kind ('accessToken=123456') FIRED true. The code DOES appear in the body of the single POST /auth/mfa/verify, which is where it belongs and is the one request that redeems it. Analytics: OpalAnalytics.init is called only from establishSession(), which runs only after a session exists, and the code is not in scope there -- the payload carries email, name, role, firmId only.
acceptance.denominator: 6 client-state carriers enumerated + 55 of 55 console messages + 1 analytics call site.
acceptance.status_reason: COVERAGE BOUND OF MY OWN GUARD, recorded because it survives the answer that the behaviour is intentional: requestMfaCode() refuses to report a code as sent when the send fails, but /auth/mfa/send answers 200 for an unknown challenge BY DESIGN, so the guarded case and the unguarded one are indistinguishable at the only layer this client can see. A deliberately uninformative response defeats a client-side guard exactly as effectively as a broken one -- the intent changes the blame, not the observability. Stated as a bound on the guard, NOT as a defect in anyone's code. POSITIVE CONTROL CARRIED because this is an ABSENCE claim, the class where a broken detector reproduces the desired answer exactly: six false results from a matcher that cannot fire would read identically to a true clean. BOUND: this enumerates the carriers readable from the page. It does not cover a browser extension, devtools history, or the network log -- the code is necessarily in the request body in transit, protected by TLS, not by this criterion.
